messages:
ops-bot: :warning: Alert: Partial degradation detected in us-west-2a - GPU host group gw-infer-g4dn reported 40% hosts unhealthy, networking flaps observed, pod evictions increasing. Alert ID: INF-2025-9673
priya: Noted. I'm oncall. Starting investigation — checking autoscaler and instance health.
alex: I'm looking at the host metrics. Looks like ENI attach errors and sporadic SSH timeouts from the hypervisor side. Networking team pinged.
jordan: Can we start zonal evacuation for non-critical Dedicated pools? We should avoid user impact for host-level failures.
mateo: Agree. Plan: drain affected nodes in us-west-2a, route new allocations to 2b/c. We'll set maxUnavailable to 20% for critical shards.
priya: Proceed with a phased drain. First drain pool: batch-infer-spot (lowest priority). Command I'll run: `kubectl drain gpu-node-az-a-03 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60`
alex: Also switch autoscaler profile to prefer 2b,c: `infra-cli prefer-az --region us-west-2 --prefer az:b,c --profile shard-infer`
elena: FYI Dedicated customers with pinned AZ will be affected. I'll message account owners and spin up standby capacity in 2b for those pinned to 2a.
casey: Product note: streaming endpoints may see increased latency while KV cache warms on new nodes. Warn PL teams and add a short blurb in status if impact >5% latency.
jordan: Routing: we'll update the smart-router policy to divert new requests away from any node with host.health!=healthy. This is non-disruptive for existing sessions.
mateo: Rebalancer will attempt automatic placement but we should cap concurrent moves to avoid throttle. Setting `max_rebalance_parallel=4`.
priya: Running drain for two low-priority nodes now, monitoring failure counts and token latency.
ops-bot: System: Evacuation job started for 2 nodes in us-west-2a (job_id evac-1752003456-01).
alex: Seeing repeated ENI detach failures on instance i-0a1b2c3d. AWS Support has a ticket opened (SR-81234). They suspect upstream AZ fabric issue.
jordan: If AWS indicates wider AZ fabric issue, we should prepare for cross-AZ capacity shortfall. Options: accelerate cross-region fallback to us-east-1 for non-latency-sensitive Dedicated shards. Thoughts?\mato (typo correction): *mateo: cross-region will add egress costs and cache cold starts. We should estimate cost and SLA impacts first.
priya: Agreed. For now keep within region. Trigger cross-region only if capacity <70% of required or >30 minutes with sustained host failures.\celena: Noted re cost. I'll pre-approve emergency extra-node allocation up to $6k/hr if we hit that threshold, to avoid customer SLA breaches.
c: (typo) *casey: Also prepare a status message template: "Partial AZ degradation in us-west-2a causing traffic rebalancing; some endpoints may see higher latency. Teams are draining affected instances."
priya: Update: drained 2/6 targeted nodes, no customer errors observed. Token latency +2ms median.
ops-bot: System: autoscaler shifted 72% of new pod placements to us-west-2b and 28% to 2c.
alex: Network team reports flaps have reduced but isolated hosts still show networking resets. We'll keep draining until all unhealthy hosts are evacuated.
jordan: After drain finishes, we'll run `rebalance --verify` to ensure even GPU utilization across AZs. Also run canary traffic to simulate 10% load on rebalanced nodes.
mateo: FYI batch jobs already queued into 2b; scheduled warmup to pre-populate KV caches.
priya: ETA for full evacuation of us-west-2a GPU pools: ~45-60 minutes assuming no new host failures.
elena: I'm drafting customer comms for impacted Dedicated customers and preparing billing holdbacks/credits logic if we need to prorate.
casey: PL teams alerted. Monitoring dashboard has a temporary card for AZ-level health and rebalancer status.
jordan: If we see more than 50% of GPU capacity in the AZ go unhealthy, escalate to SEV-2 and start cross-region fallback.
priya: Final status update in ~30m or earlier if conditions change. Also tagging incidents channel: #incidents for postmortem link. :thumbsup:
